facts.raw_span: asymptomatic erythematous scaly plaques over the face and proximal extremities
involvement of the upper respiratory tract, causing palatal perforation and stridor, necessitating a tracheostomy a year ago
no history of preceding trauma, fever, malaise, joint pain, cough, epistaxis, hemoptysis, or hematuria
multiple well-defined brown erythematous scaly plaques with central scarring measuring 2 × 1 to 8 × 7 cm on the face, arm, and thighs
saddle nose deformity, perforation of the hard palate, and necrotic plaques on the ear with destruction of ear cartilage
cervical lymphadenopathy: multiple, nontender, discrete nodes, ranging from 1.5 to 2 cm without surface changes
anemia (hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL)
normal kidney function test
normal liver function test
infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation (Fontana-Masson)
pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, foamy histiocytes, neutrophils, and multinucleate giant cells along with pigmented hyphae
fungal skin culture: black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions and fungal culture results are consistent with chromoblastomycosis, a fungal infection caused by Exophiala spinifera.
The patient has a saddle nose deformity, which is a common complication of chronic granulomatous infections or inflammatory conditions.
The patient has a history of palatal perforation, which is a complication of upper respiratory tract involvement.
The patient has anemia, which may be related to chronic infection or inflammation.
The patient has cervical lymphadenopathy, which is a common finding in chronic infections or inflammatory conditions.
The patient's fungal culture results are consistent with Exophiala spinifera infection.
The patient's histopathology results are consistent with chronic granulomatous disease, which may be related to the patient's fungal infection.
The patient has destructive lesions of the ear, which is a complication of chronic granulomatous infections or inflammatory conditions.
The patient has a history of upper respiratory tract infection, which may be related to the patient's fungal infection.
The patient has chronic inflammation, which is a common finding in chronic infections or inflammatory conditions.
